context.title: Field Notes: Running a Small Home Server

items.text: To install the CLI, run
npm install -g fernctl
and then check the version with
fernctl --version
. Version 2.4.1 or later is required.
The
timeout
option accepts a value in milliseconds; the default is 30000 (30 seconds), and setting it to 0 disables the limit entirely.
Before upgrading from v1.x, back up your
configuration directory
because the migration script rewrites every file in place and cannot be undone.
If the daemon fails to start, make sure port 8443 is not already bound by another process. You can inspect the logs at http://localhost:8443/debug/logs.
Each worker thread keeps its own cache of roughly 64 MB, so a machine with 8 GB of RAM should not run more than eight workers.
Requests are retried up to three times with exponential backoff; if all attempts fail, the error is surfaced to the caller as a
TransientError

Last spring I decided to turn an old laptop into a home server for my family's photos.
The laptop, a 2014
ThinkBook
with 8 GB of RAM, turned out to be perfect for the job.
First, I installed
Debian 12
and set up a small web app called Fernbox to browse the pictures.
My sister was skeptical at first, but after a week she admitted that Fernbox was faster than any cloud service she had used.
Now the old laptop sits quietly on a shelf, and
Fernbox
has become the first thing my whole family opens after a trip.
